sentences.text: Dromiceiomimus was a fast bipedal runner that closely resembled a modern running bird.
This animal measured approximately 3.5 meters in length and weighed between 100 and 150 kilograms.
Its anatomy featured long hind legs, large eye sockets, and a toothless beak.
The creature possessed a short neck and back, with the spine length before the pelvis being shorter than the combined length of the hind leg even without the toes.
The skull of Dromiceiomimus was very elongated.
The toothless lower jaw was also elongated and very thin.
The vertebral column consists of ten cervical vertebrae, thirteen dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and approximately thirty-five tail vertebrae.
The transition point between the front and rear tail vertebrae occurs before the fourteenth vertebra.
Dromiceiomimus was one of the fastest dinosaurs, capable of reaching speeds of 70 kilometers per hour to escape predators like Gorgosaurus.
Some estimates compare its maximum speed to that of an ostrich, suggesting it could exceed 70 kilometers per hour.
Large eye sockets suggest a highly developed sense of vision, giving the possibility that it was nocturnal.
The genus Dromiceiomimus was named by Russell in 1972.
Nicholls and Russell cast doubt on the validity of Dromiceiomimus in 1981, arguing that limb proportions were insufficient to distinguish it from other ornithomimids.
In 2018, McDonald and Currie rejected the synonymization of Dromiceiomimus with Ornithomimus, citing significant differences in thighbone/shinbone ratios.
It is believed that Dromiceiomimus was warm-blooded and likely had primitive feathers to stay warm.
Ornithomimids had large brains for dinosaurs, though some paleontologists suggest these were dedicated to movement coordination rather than high intelligence.
Dromiceiomimus was presumably omnivorous and would eat small animals if the opportunity arose.
Canadian paleontologist Dale Russell suggested that these animals were entirely carnivorous, feeding on eggs and small animals they could pull from burrows with their long arms.
It could have eaten insects, fruits, eggs, lizards, and small mammals.
The jaw articulation allowed front-to-back movement, suggesting its beak could easily cut plant material while staying sharp through wear.
The vertical bite force of Dromiceiomimus was likely small.
Dromiceiomimus belongs to the parent group Ornithomimidae.
Dromiceiomimus is classified within the family Ornithomimidae.
Dromiceiomimus is classified under the class Reptilia.
Dromiceiomimus was placed within Ornithomimidae by Russell.
Russell renamed Ornithomimus samueli as the second species of Dromiceiomimus, Dromiceiomimus samueli.
Dromiceiomimus samueli is recognized as a subdivision or species within the genus.
The relationship with other Ornithomimus species is not yet entirely clear.
Dromiceiomimus lived during the Late Cretaceous (early Maastrichtian) in Alberta, Canada.
Dromiceiomimus originated in the early Maastrichtian, distinguishing it from Ornithomimus species which originated in the late Maastrichtian.
Dromiceiomimus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Makovicky et al. claimed there is no statistical support for distinguishing Dromiceiomimus from Ornithomimus and synonymized it with Ornithomimus edmontonicus.
Some authors, including Longrich, continued to treat Dromiceiomimus as a valid genus distinct from Ornithomimus.
It is debated whether the differences between Dromiceiomimus brevitertius and Dromiceiomimus samueli are distinct enough to warrant separate species status.
Researchers suggest that the heavier skull of Dromiceiomimus samueli might be due to allometry rather than a true species difference, as its holotype is larger.
This opinion regarding a purely carnivorous diet is still under discussion, as its body shape suggests an adaptation for a partially herbivorous lifestyle.
